Duh. Most places have dozens of Level 1 and 2 workers who are literally only trained to handle the most basic support calls, and will have a handful, or sometimes as few as one Level 3 . That's why the first guy you talk to always runs you through a "bottom-up" script. That means no matter what you say or what solutions you say you've already tried, he is going to start at the absolute most basic diagnostic or solution and work up from there until the problem is fixed or he reaches the end of his skillset. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, bottom-up has its place and 9 times out of 10 it's the right way to work, but being insistent and ignoring customer input in favor of the script is shit and a direct result of breaking your support team into fractured skill tiers. That guy at the top gets paid way more than the first guy you talk to, so they have a vested interest in not wasting his time with support issues that can be handled (even if it's poorly) by people getting paid much less than him, which is why they do everything they can to stop you from talking to him as long as they can.

I look for online live chats now. I've always found that less infuriating than talking on the phone and since it's way easier to outsource (which I don't give a shit about since I don't have to deal with the accent), they usually have more workers and you don't wait as long.
